# Manuscript Figures Gallery (Figs. 1–4) {#figures}

```{r ch9-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
fd <- get_final_data(); eco <- get_eco()
```

Every manuscript figure is assembled programmatically in R (`patchwork` + `R/ternary.R` + `R/figures.R`) and written to `figs/` as 300 dpi PNG and vector PDF files.

---

## Figure 1: Continental Data Distributions and Ecoregion Coverage {#fig1}

```{r fig1, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9.5}
p1 <- fig1(fd, eco)
save_fig(p1, 'fig1_distributions_map', 11, 9.5)
p1
```

* **(a)** Kernel density distributions of `Chl a` ($\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$), `DOC` ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$), `Secchi` ($\text{m}$), and `TSS` ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) by water-body type (`Estuary`, `Lake`, `Stream`) across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`** application observations, contrasting samples with measured Secchi depth (`Measured`, solid lines; $n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$secchi_status == 'Measured'))`$) against samples where Secchi depth is modeled by Model 7 (`Modeled`, dashed lines; $n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$secchi_status == 'Modeled'))`$) using the consistent pure-water offset $k_w = `r round(get_k_w(), 5)`\text{ m}^{-1}$.
* **(b)** Spatial density of simultaneous observations aggregated to $0.1^\circ \times 0.1^\circ$ grid cells over U.S. EPA Level III ecoregions.

---

## Figure 2: Continental Ternary Partitioning by Water-Body Type {#fig2}

```{r fig2, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8.4}
p2 <- fig2(fd)
save_fig(p2, 'fig2_ternary_by_type', 9, 8.4)
p2
```

Individual points represent per-sample non-water light-attenuation fractions $(f_{\text{Chl }a}, f_{\text{DOC}}, f_{\text{NAP}})$ predicted by Model 7 across **(a)** all water types ($n = `r fmt_n(nrow(fd))`$), **(b)** streams ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Stream'))`$), **(c)** lakes ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Lake'))`$), and **(d)** estuaries ($n = `r fmt_n(sum(fd$type == 'Estuary'))`$). Blue circles mark arithmetic mean compositions; red and black polygons enclose the exact simplex regions within $\pm 1\text{ SD}$ and $\pm 2\text{ SD}$ of each group mean (`tern_sd_region()`).

---

## Figure 3: Longitudinal River–Estuary Continuum Along the Delaware River and Bay {#fig3}

```{r fig3, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.6}
f3 <- get_fig3_data()
p3 <- fig3(f3)
save_fig(p3, 'fig3_delaware', 13, 5.6)
p3
```

Longitudinal shift in light-attenuation partitioning along **231 km** of the Delaware River and Delaware Bay across **`r nrow(f3$sites)`** Delaware River Basin Commission (`31DELRBC_WQX`) long-term monitoring stations with $\ge `r P$long_term_min_years`$ distinct years of data (`r f3$years[1]`–`r f3$years[2]`). Because Model 7 assigns attenuation coefficients by Level III ecoregion (`8.5.1` Middle Atlantic Coastal Plain for Sites 1–5; `8.5.4` Atlantic Coastal Pine Barrens at the bay mouth for Site 6) without imposing an artificial categorical break between `Stream` and `Estuary`, it seamlessly resolves the continuum from **DOC dominance** in the tidal freshwater river at Trenton (`Site 1, 0 km`) through increasing **NAP dominance** along the upper and lower tidal river (`Sites 2–4, 41–123 km`, classified as `Stream` in WQP) to **DOC–NAP co-dominance and interannual switching** driven by tidal and wind resuspension in Delaware Bay (`Sites 5–6, 180–231 km`, classified as `Estuary` in WQP).

```{r fig3-table}
f3$sites %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% inner_join(DELAWARE_EXEMPLARS, by = 'SiteID') %>%
  left_join(f3$year_avg %>% group_by(SiteID) %>%
              summarize(years = paste(min(year), max(year), sep = '–'),
                        n_years = n(),
                        mean_DOC = percent(mean(doc_kd), 0.1),
                        mean_NAP = percent(mean(tss_kd), 0.1),
                        mean_Chl = percent(mean(chl_kd), 0.1)),
            by = 'SiteID') %>%
  select(num, SiteID, label, type, dist_trenton, years, n_years, mean_DOC, mean_NAP, mean_Chl) %>%
  kable(digits = 0, col.names = c('Panel #', 'WQP SiteID', 'Panel Title', 'WQP Type', 'Distance from Trenton (km)', 'Years Sampled', 'Distinct Years', 'Mean DOC %', 'Mean NAP %', 'Mean Chl a %'),
        caption = 'Long-term Delaware River and Bay monitoring stations highlighted in Panels 1–6 of Figure 3.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

## Figure 4: Site-Level Temporal Stability — Lucistatic vs. Lucidynamic Regimes {#fig4}

```{r fig4, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 6.8}
areas <- get_fig4_areas()
p4 <- fig4(fd, areas)
save_fig(p4, 'fig4_area_cdf', 9.5, 6.8)
p4
```

For each monitoring station with $> `r P$fig4_min_obs`$ simultaneous observations (**`r fmt_n(nrow(areas))` sites** across the conterminous U.S.), the **ternary area fraction** (`tern_area_fraction()`) is the exact area of its $\pm 2\text{ SD}$ simplex polygon (clipped to $[0, 1]^3$ via Sutherland–Hodgman half-plane clipping) divided by the total area of the equilateral unit-side triangle ($\sqrt{3}/4 \approx 0.4330$). Empirical cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) by water-body type demonstrate that streams (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Stream']), 0.1)`**) and estuaries (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Estuary']), 0.1)`**) are more temporally concentrated in ternary space (*lucistatic*) than lakes (median **`r percent(median(areas$area[areas$type == 'Lake']), 0.1)`**, *lucidynamic*). Fewer than **5%** of lakes (`4.5%`) and fewer than **2%** of streams (`1.6%`) and estuaries (`0.4%`) occupy $\ge 50\%$ of ternary space.

### Summary of Figure 4 CDFs and Exemplar Stations {#fig4-sites}

```{r fig4-medians}
areas %>%
  group_by(`Water-Body Type` = type) %>%
  summarize(
    `Sites (> 7 obs)` = fmt_n(n()),
    `25th Percentile` = percent(quantile(area, 0.25), 0.1),
    `Median Area Fraction` = percent(median(area), 0.1),
    `Mean Area Fraction` = percent(mean(area), 0.1),
    `75th Percentile` = percent(quantile(area, 0.75), 0.1),
    `% Sites >= 50% Area` = percent(mean(area >= 0.50), 0.1)
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'Distribution of site-level ternary area fractions across water-body types (Figure 4 CDFs).') %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'))
```

```{r fig4-sites}
FIG4_SITES %>%
  left_join(areas, by = 'SiteID') %>%
  transmute(
    Inset = inset,
    `CDF Label` = label,
    `WQP SiteID` = SiteID,
    `Station Name` = site_name,
    `Water Type` = type,
    `Observations (n)` = n,
    `Ternary Area Fraction` = percent(area, 0.1),
    `CDF Percentile` = percent(map2_dbl(type, area, ~ ecdf(areas$area[areas$type == .x])(.y)), 0.1),
    `Optical Regime` = role
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = 'The five exemplar monitoring stations highlighted on the CDF curves and Insets 1–3 of Figure 4.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), font_size = 12, full_width = TRUE)
```
